descriptors.definition: Propriety audit evaluates public sector transactions against standards of public interest, financial prudence, and economy rather than mere formal regulatory compliance. It examines executive decisions to uncover wasteful, avoidable, or infructuous expenditures by applying the standard of ordinary prudence to public money.
inclusion: Scrutiny of executive actions based on financial prudence
Detection of wasteful or infructuous spending
Evaluation of transactions against standards of public morality and custom
exclusion: Strict mechanical checking of vouchers and documents without substance review
Exclusive focus on procedural formalities of rules and regulations
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from regularity audit because a transaction may fully comply with formal rules yet still fail propriety tests due to wastefulness.

descriptors.concept_name: Audit Report Of The Comptroller And Auditor General
descriptors.definition: The Comptroller and Auditor General presents structured reports on public sector undertakings to Parliament and state legislatures in multiple segments. These reports include reviews of working results, comprehensive appraisals by the audit board, statutory auditor report summaries, and specific findings on financial irregularities.
inclusion: General review of government company working results
Results of comprehensive appraisals of selected undertakings
Resume of company auditors' reports and accounts comments
Significant audit results of undertakings not selected for appraisal
exclusion: Primary statutory audit execution performed directly by initial company auditors without C&AG oversight
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from individual statutory audit reports by providing a consolidated and structured legislative overview of public sector financial performance and irregularities.
